Messages.Author: Jim Vamp
Messages.Body:
Question: Meth. A bleeds meth. B, who says "okay". Meth A then throws
down a +3 modifier. Can meth B AT THIS POINT redirect the bleed to
meth C since he already allowed the bleed?

Confirmation: Sudden reversal can only be played when the master card to
be reversed is played, right? I.E. meth A plays a hunting ground, then
begins to do his actions. Meth B tries to pull a sudden reversal after
the action phase has started. Too late right? (he was given ample time
to play the reversal during the master phase).

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <4b7ju4$q...@news.paonline.com>, jim....@paonline.com (Jim
"Vamp") wrote:

: Question: Meth. A bleeds meth. B, who says "okay". Meth A then throws

: down a +3 modifier. Can meth B AT THIS POINT redirect the bleed to
: meth C since he already allowed the bleed?

Sure thing. The only thing the blocking Meth has given up is the right to
block the action. S/he may still reduced the bleed or redirect it.

: Confirmation: Sudden reversal can only be played when the master card to

: be reversed is played, right? I.E. meth A plays a hunting ground, then
: begins to do his actions. Meth B tries to pull a sudden reversal after
: the action phase has started. Too late right? (he was given ample time
: to play the reversal during the master phase).

Correct. Sudden Reversal must be played when the master card is being
played. So, if the Meth wanting to use the SR does not have it during the
Master Phase, then the Hunting Groud comes out. However, it is important
to remember that Meths have an opportunity to react to everything another
Meth does. If the Meth wanting to SR has it, s/he is always given the
opportunity to use it, you can't just play the card and move on to
actions, trying to make sure that it can't be SRed.

I hope this helps

stephen beaulieu

Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:
jim....@paonline.com (Jim "Vamp") wrote:
>Question: Meth. A bleeds meth. B, who says "okay". Meth A then throws
>down a +3 modifier. Can meth B AT THIS POINT redirect the bleed to
>meth C since he already allowed the bleed?

Peace Jim,

Yes, Meth B may Deflect/Misdirect a bleed after a modifer has been played
even if s/h/it did not block.

>Confirmation: Sudden reversal can only be played when the master card to
>be reversed is played, right? I.E. meth A plays a hunting ground, then
>begins to do his actions. Meth B tries to pull a sudden reversal after
>the action phase has started. Too late right? (he was given ample time
>to play the reversal during the master phase).

Yes, SR must be used 'immediately', but Meth A cannot "speed play", i.e.:
fail to allow all other players sufficient time to respond to the Master
card play before proceeding to Minion Phase.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
jim....@paonline.com (Jim "Vamp") writes:
>Question: Meth. A bleeds meth. B, who says "okay". Meth A then throws
>down a +3 modifier. Can meth B AT THIS POINT redirect the bleed to
>meth C since he already allowed the bleed?

Yes. He didn't "allow" the bleed - he simply declined to "block" the
bleed. He could even say - "I don't block - do you wish to
play any action modifiers before I begin playing reactions?"

But that takes a little longer than "okay" :-)

>Confirmation: Sudden reversal can only be played when the master card to
>be reversed is played, right? I.E. meth A plays a hunting ground, then
>begins to do his actions. Meth B tries to pull a sudden reversal after
>the action phase has started. Too late right? (he was given ample time
>to play the reversal during the master phase).

Correct. So long as he's given opportunity, he's out of luck. If he
needs more time to decide, he should say "wait" or somesuch.
